source: Provincial open data; see each province for its own source and licence
note: Canada has no national equivalent to the United States' HPMS. These are the five provinces that publish route-level traffic counts in bulk, each in its own form and under its own terms. British Columbia, Saskatchewan and Manitoba publish only through maps, applications or PDFs; the remaining jurisdictions do not publish machine-readable counts. Figures are joined to routes by the province's route number, never by position.

QC.source: Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, Débit de circulation

ON.source: Ontario Ministry of Transportation, Provincial Highways Traffic Volumes
ON.licence: no licence stated by the publisher
ON.note: Where two Ontario highways overlap, the ministry credits the volume to the lower-numbered one, or to the freeway where a freeway and a non-freeway meet.

AB.source: Alberta Transportation and Economic Corridors, Traffic volumes on links in the highway network

NS.source: Nova Scotia Department of Public Works, Traffic Volumes – Provincial Highway System
NS.note: The province counts one direction at a time. Opposite directions are added, each from the most recent time it was counted, to give a two-way volume comparable with the other provinces; a location counted in one direction only is excluded. Speeds are the 85th percentile.

NB.source: New Brunswick Department of Transportation and Infrastructure, AADT counts at point locations on the DTI highway network
